subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & regulatory constraints for ACME Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Carter <sophie.carter@acmehealth.com>, Luis Ramirez <luis.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Private/VPC options & regulatory constraints for ACME Health

Hi Sophie + Luis — great to meet you both on the call just now. Thanks for walking us through ACME Health's priorities. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we all have the same expectations.

Summary of pain points / constraints:
- Regulatory & residency: PHI must remain in US-only accounts; ACME requires SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA BAAs, and proof of data residency controls. No cross-border replication.
- Networking & air-gap: Primary preference is a Private/VPC deployment in our AWS GovCloud or customer-managed VPC; on-prem appliance is required for a small set of legacy systems currently in an air-gapped environment.
- Connectivity: VPC peering and private link preferred; customer cannot expose inference endpoints on public internet for PHI traffic.
- Latency & throughput: Real-time clinical workflows require 100–150ms p95 for short (<=512 token) prompts; expected peak 75 RPS for the first rollout.
- Audit & visibility: Need audit logs, KMS integration, and per-tenant access controls for compliance reviews.

What we propose (next steps):
1) I'll share our private deployment architecture diagram and a short Mutual Action Plan (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Vivek to align on network design (VPC peering, PrivateLink, firewall rules) and on-prem appliance requirements.
3) Send SOC 2 / HIPAA artifacts and our standard BAA template to your security team.
4) Pricing: we'll scope Dedicated/Private pricing after the technical deep-dive — I'll include an estimated budget range in the MAP by EOD Wednesday.

Immediate asks from ACME: please confirm the following so we can prep:
- Which AWS regions (account IDs) will we deploy into? (GovCloud, us-east-1, etc.)
- Any existing IP allowlist or proxy that requires explicit rules?
- Who from your security/compliance team should we loop in for SOC 2 artifact exchange?

Attachments: redwood-private-architecture.pdf (high-level), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline & owners).

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive: Wed 03/24 09:00–10:00 PT or Thu 03/25 11:00–12:00 PT — open to other slots.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect, appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Regions: Primary will be us-east-1 (non-GovCloud) for clinical apps, but for certain regulated workloads we may need GovCloud or a true on-prem appliance — we'll confirm exact account IDs by EOD tomorrow.
- Air-gap: The legacy telemetry pipeline is air-gapped; we can't forward PHI from that environment. For that subset, we will need an on-prem containerized runtime or an isolated appliance.
- Security contact: Tom Nguyen (cc'd) will handle SOC 2 artifacts and the BAA. Tom, please confirm what format you prefer for artifact exchange.
- Timeline: Procurement is targeting an SOW in Q2; tightest deadline for a pilot is end of May.

We can do the technical deep-dive on Wed 03/24 09:00 PT. Vivek — can you take that session? We'd like it to focus on network flow, KMS key management, and the appliance capability.

Sophie
Sophie Carter
Director, IT Architecture, ACME Health
